articles.title: Deshaun Watson avoids disaster, returns to Browns-Steelers matchup after concussion check
articles.standfirst: The Cleveland quarterback briefly exited Sunday's crucial AFC North clash following a penalty against Jaquan Brisker
articles.summary: The Cleveland quarterback briefly exited Sunday's crucial AFC North clash following a penalty against Jaquan Brisker
articles.body:
D eshaun Watson 's return to prominence with the Cleveland Browns faced another potential setback on Sunday when a frightening hit against the Pittsburgh Steelers forced the quarterback to leave the field for a concussion evaluation.

The 31-year-old was struck in the helmet by Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker during Cleveland's opening possession at Acrisure Stadium, immediately raising concerns about his availability for one of the Browns ' most important divisional games of the season.

Brisker was penalized for roughing the passer after making contact with Watson's head as the quarterback released the football. Watson initially remained on the ground before getting to his feet and heading toward the sideline.

Medical personnel directed him into the blue evaluation tent, leaving backup Shedeur Sanders to take control of Cleveland's offense while Watson underwent concussion checks.

However, the Browns received encouraging news within minutes when Watson emerged from the tent, collected his helmet and returned for the team's second offensive possession after clearing the evaluation.

Sanders ' unexpected introduction provided another opportunity for the young quarterback, who has spent much of the season behind Watson on Cleveland's depth chart.

The former Colorado standout completed both passing attempts for two yards during his brief appearance, but the possession ended when tight end Harold Fannin Jr. lost a fumble.

Watson 's return ensured Sanders ' opportunity lasted only one series, allowing head coach Todd Monken to continue with the quarterback who had helped Cleveland establish a 5-2 record entering Week 8.

The veteran's performances have been instrumental in the Browns ' improved results, particularly after a difficult period for the franchise that raised questions about its long-term quarterback situation.

Watson entered Sunday's contest having completed 64.8 percent of his passes for 1,482 yards, while contributing eight total touchdowns against three interceptions.

He had also played an important role in Cleveland's 27-24 victory over Pittsburgh earlier in the season, completing 24 of 33 passes for 268 yards and a touchdown.

Injury relief overshadowed by difficult Steelers defeat

Although Watson avoided an extended absence, his return didn't prevent Cleveland from enduring another difficult afternoon against its AFC North rival.

The quarterback's problems continued shortly after reentering the contest, when he lost a fumble on a sack that handed Pittsburgh favorable field position.

The Steelers capitalized on Cleveland's mistakes and eventually secured a convincing 27-6 victory, moving ahead of the Browns in the divisional standings.

Despite the disappointing result, Watson 's successful concussion evaluation represented an important development for Monken, whose offense has relied on the veteran throughout the campaign.

Sanders remains Cleveland's primary backup, while Dillon Gabriel was designated the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game.

The Browns will now assess their performance after a damaging divisional defeat, although the immediate concern surrounding Watson's availability was resolved before the opening quarter had finished.

His return prevented an unexpected quarterback change from becoming another significant complication for a team attempting to remain in the AFC playoff race.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders could get golden opportunity to steal Deshaun Watson's starting QB job
articles.standfirst: Watson hasn't thrown a touchdown pass since October 11.
articles.summary: Watson hasn't thrown a touchdown pass since October 11.
articles.body:
There weren't many fans who thought the Cleveland Browns would be sporting a 5-3 record midway through first-time head coach Todd Monken 's debut season. The Browns have outperformed expectations, fueled by a stout defense and success in one-score games.

Week 8 was a bit of a wake-up call, though. Playing against their AFC North rivals, Cleveland got walloped 27-6 by the Pittsburgh Steelers in a game that was never truly close. The offense, in particular, struggled mightily. For the third straight game, quarterback Deshaun Watson failed to throw a single touchdown pass, while also taking eight sacks .

Shedeur Sanders could start in Week 9 if Deshaun Watson doesn't clear concussion protocol

Getting hit so many times appears to have shaken up Watson, as he has entered the concussion protocol in the lead-up to Week 9 . Developing concussion symptoms after a game is usually not a great sign for a player's availability for the next game. That means Shedeur Sanders could very well be the Browns' starting quarterback against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.

If he does get the nod, this could be a golden opportunity for Sanders. While Watson hasn't been an outright disaster, by almost all metrics, he's been one of the worst starting quarterbacks in the league. Both PFF (grade) and ESPN (QBR) have him ranked as the 28th-best QB in the NFL this season . If Sanders can move the ball through the air more efficiently and dynamically than Watson on Sunday, it might give Monken something to think about going forward.

Many expected Sanders to make starts at some point this season. That was believed to be the plan if the Browns looked to be going nowhere, but at 5-3, Sanders simply hasn't gotten the chance to make a case for the starting job. Replacing an injured Watson is the platform Sanders needs, but he must deliver.

articles.title: Is Todd Monken letting Shedeur Sanders know what he expects from him, or putting pressure on him?
articles.standfirst: After Deshaun Watson's injury, all eyes are on Shedeur Sanders—and Todd Monken has already laid out his expectations.
articles.summary: After Deshaun Watson's injury, all eyes are on Shedeur Sanders—and Todd Monken has already laid out his expectations.
articles.body:
Shedeur Sanders ’ first passes in the 2026 NFL season have not been the most impressive. The Cleveland Browns quarterback has made only two appearances, both coming in as a backup for Deshaun Watson when the starter had to leave the field due to injury: in Week 3 against Carolina and in Week 8 against the Steelers .

In total, Sanders has participated in just five plays this year, but he has completed all three of his pass attempts for a mere two yards. Still, coach Todd Monken believes the circumstances under which the young quarterback has entered the games have not been ideal, though he acknowledges that is one of the responsibilities of an NFL backup.

After it was confirmed that Deshaun Watson suffered a concussion from Jaquan Brisker’s hit in the first quarter of the most recent game, forcing him to leave the field, Monken made it clear that he trusts Sanders and is excited about the possibility of him getting a larger opportunity.

Todd Monken trusts Shedeur Sanders

Far from appearing concerned about Watson’s absence, Monken said he is motivated by the chance to see Sanders take control of the offense and show what he can contribute.

I can’t wait. It’s so cool. I mean, that’s an opportunity. If it goes that way, then he gets a great opportunity, right, to go play, right? And for us to see him go play. And, you know, again, I don’t know how Deshaun will feel tomorrow. I’m excited for today. I’m excited for us to go out there today.

Monken also highlighted Sanders’ preparation during training camp and noted that depth at the quarterback position is exactly why teams work with their backups.

“… And I can’t wait to see him let it rip today and see where we’re at. I mean, that’s what you do. That’s why you build depth. That’s why he got a ton of reps in fall camp. I mean, that’s really the benefit of all this, is when we opened it up as a competition, he got a ton of those reps.”

Browns will stick with their offensive plan with Sanders

Sanders has been one of the most discussed names in Cleveland in recent weeks after competing for the starting quarterback job during the spring and summer before the team ultimately chose Watson in late August .

With Dillon Gabriel returning from injured reserve, rumors emerged about the possibility that one of the two quarterbacks — Gabriel or Sanders — could be traded, though sources close to the Browns have ruled out that option.

Looking ahead to a possible appearance by Sanders , Monken said Cleveland will not make drastic changes to its offensive scheme, although he acknowledged there are differences between the two players’ styles.

“I don’t think so. I don’t see the way, because the rest of the guys are the same, and they’re similar in some ways. Some things, you know, Shedeur’s skill set is different than Deshaun’s, but still very similar in terms of what we do. We can’t change that dramatically.”

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders fires back at reporter over agent question as Browns face QB decision
articles.standfirst: Deshaun Watson’s concussion status could put Sanders in line for his first start of 2026
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson’s concussion status could put Sanders in line for his first start of 2026
articles.body:
Shedeur Sanders pushed back at a reporter who asked why he recently hired an agent, saying, “What’s that have to do with this game?” The exchange came Wednesday, four days before Cleveland’s game against the New Orleans Saints, as the Browns waited to see whether Deshaun Watson could play.

Sanders signed with agent Adie von Gontard, CEO of Young Money APAA Sports, on Oct. 14. He had gone through the 2025 NFL Draft and the early part of his pro career without an agent. His former Colorado teammate Travis Hunter is also represented by von Gontard’s agency. Sanders has not publicly explained why he made the move, and there is no confirmation that it signals a trade.

Sanders could start if Watson cannot play

Earlier in the news conference, Shedeur struck a more appreciative tone, thanking the Browns’ coaching staff, general manager Andrew Berry and the organization for giving him another opportunity.

He said his rookie season showed him what he needed to improve and that he worked on those areas during the offseason and training camp. “Overall, I’m just excited for the opportunity,” Sanders said.

Shedeur Sanders has seen little regular-season action this year. He has appeared in two games, completing all three of his pass attempts for two yards. In Sunday’s 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, he played four offensive snaps and went 2-for-2 for two yards.

As a rookie in 2025, he appeared in eight games and started seven, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

Deshaun Watson entered concussion protocol after reporting symptoms that began Monday night, two days after a helmet-to-helmet hit against Pittsburgh. He did not practice Wednesday, and Shedeur took the first-team reps.

Monken had not ruled Watson out, however, and said he would “assume” Watson remained the starter if cleared.

The Browns were preparing Sanders in case Watson could not play, making him the likely starter for Sunday, Nov. 8, in New Orleans. If Watson is cleared, he is expected to remain the starter. Cleveland’s next game after the Saints is scheduled for Nov. 15 against the Houston Texans.

articles.title: Shilo Sanders explains Shedeur's "immature" moment with Browns reporter before Saints game
articles.standfirst: Shedeur is expected to start in Week 9 if Deshaun Watson doesn't clear the concussion protocol.
articles.summary: Shedeur is expected to start in Week 9 if Deshaun Watson doesn't clear the concussion protocol.
articles.body:
As of right now, with the Cleveland Browns vs. New Orleans Saints game just a few days away, it's unclear who the starting quarterback will be for head coach Todd Monken . Deshaun Watson is still in the concussion protocol, meaning Shedeur Sanders would be next up if the starter can't go on Sunday.

This would be Sanders' first start since the final game of the 2025 season. The second-year player got beat out by Watson over the summer in the Browns' quarterback competition. Now, he'll get his chance to show he should have been the pick from the get-go.

As the game nears, Sanders has once again started to get more media attention, since he looks more and more likely to be the starter. That led to one somewhat awkward moment with longtime Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot this week.

Shedeur Sanders once again the subject of criticism for moment with Browns reporter

Cabot asked Sanders what he had seen on film from the Saints defense that stood out to him, and Sanders began laughing before opining: " Yeah, I've seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means… something. I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying? I'm maturing. I could have gave that a decent answer. Now I'm just gonna smile when it's some questions, you know. "

Sanders' response drew criticism, with many calling him " immature " or " dumb ". His brother, Shilo Sanders , came out to clear the air on the situation and explain why Shedeur couldn't help but laugh.

" Has he studied the Saints defense? That's probably why he's laughing. It's like, bruh, what do you think we go there and do every morning in meetings? "

Shedeur hasn't had the best relationship with some reporters, and Cabot is certainly one who likes poking the bear a little bit. They have a bit of a contentious history together since Shedeur joined the Browns.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders gets major blow before first Browns start as key offensive weapon suffers injury
articles.standfirst: Shedeur Sanders is preparing for his first start with the Browns, but Cleveland’s rookie quarterback could be without his most productive offensive weapon against the Saints.
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders is preparing for his first start with the Browns, but Cleveland’s rookie quarterback could be without his most productive offensive weapon against the Saints.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns could turn to Shedeur Sanders as their starting quarterback against the New Orleans Saints , but they face uncertainty about whether their top offensive weapon will be fully healthy.

Tight end Harold Fannin Jr. appeared on the injury report for the first time on Thursday with a groin issue, adding another concern for an offense already preparing to play without Deshaun Watson .

Fannin was listed as a limited participant in Thursday’s practice after not appearing on Wednesday’s initial report. Cleveland has not yet assigned him an official game designation, so Friday’s report will be key in determining his chances of playing.

The injury does not mean the tight end is ruled out for Sunday, but his history forces the Browns to proceed with caution. Fannin missed the end of his rookie season after aggravating a groin injury during a touchdown catch in Week 17 . The initial discomfort occurred in a practice before that game, and he later required offseason surgery before returning for training camp.

The situation comes at a difficult time for Cleveland, which is looking to bounce back from a 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers . Watson missed his second consecutive practice while remaining in the concussion protocol, leaving Shedeur Sanders as the primary option to make his first start of the season.

Harold Fannin arrives after his best NFL performance

Concern over Fannin’s injury comes right after the best game of his young career.

Against Pittsburgh, the tight end delivered a career performance with 10 catches for 154 yards — both personal bests. He also hauled in a 37-yard reception, though the Browns were unable to convert his production into points.

Through eight games, Fannin leads Cleveland with 35 receptions and 411 receiving yards, along with three touchdowns.

His impact has grown significantly in recent weeks. Before his breakout against the Steelers, he recorded six catches for 91 yards against Tennessee, totaling 245 receiving yards over his last two games.

“Harold is an improving player, really good hands, run after catch. He’s a bull,” coach Todd Monken said Monday. “He’s only going to continue to get better as a blocker. So it behooves us to try and get him the ball more often.”

Fannin’s development has given Cleveland a key piece alongside rookie receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston. A possible absence or limited role for the tight end would be a significant blow for Sanders, especially since he is one of the few offensive players with prior chemistry with the young quarterback.

Browns reshape their tight end group

Fannin’s situation became even more relevant after Cleveland made a move at the position.

The Browns released rookie Carsen Ryan just one day after elevating him from the practice squad, leaving Fannin and Blake Whiteheart as the only active tight ends on the 53-man roster .

John FitzPatrick remains on the practice squad, while rookie Joe Royer continues on the reserve/non-football illness list.

Ryan had appeared in seven games this season, and Cleveland did not immediately announce a replacement to fill his roster spot.

If Fannin is unable to play or is limited, Whiteheart could take on a much larger role against the Saints . The franchise will also need to evaluate whether it needs to add another tight end for greater depth at the position.

As Sanders prepares for a potential first career start, Fannin’s physical status will be one of the key factors in determining how many tools the young quarterback will have at his disposal.

articles.title: “I pray that Shedeur gets a chance somewhere else”: The injustice plaguing Deion Sanders’ son
articles.standfirst: Skip Bayless has questioned how NFL teams evaluated the former Colorado quarterback
articles.summary: Skip Bayless has questioned how NFL teams evaluated the former Colorado quarterback
articles.body:
Shedeur Sanders may be preparing for his first NFL start of the season, but Skip Bayless believes the Cleveland Browns quarterback is still paying the price for the reputation that contributed to his dramatic fall in the 2025 NFL Draft.

The former Colorado star has spent much of his second professional season backing up Deshaun Watson , having lost the starting competition during training camp despite gaining valuable experience as a rookie.

However, Watson 's placement in concussion protocol has created an unexpected opportunity for Sanders , who has been taking first-team practice repetitions ahead of Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

The development has prompted Bayless to revisit one of the most controversial stories from last year's draft, when Sanders slipped to the fifth round despite entering the process with considerable expectations.

Rather than accepting the quarterback's draft position as a reflection of his football ability, Bayless believes concerns about his personality influenced how teams evaluated him.

His criticism comes as Sanders prepares for a potentially significant moment in his career, with Cleveland attempting to improve on its 5-3 record.

Bayless delivered an emphatic defense of Sanders, arguing that the quarterback should have been considered for the first overall selection instead of Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward .

"What happened to Shedeur [Sanders] in his draft was the biggest draft injustice I have ever experienced," Bayless said. "I thought he should go No.1 to the Titans instead of Cam Ward."

The analyst suggested that Sanders ' confidence and perceived attitude during the pre-draft process worked against him, despite the performances he produced while playing under his father, Deion Sanders , at Colorado.

"He fell to the fifth round because people didn't like his style, the way he interviewed at the NFL Combine, his alleged arrogance," Bayless continued.

"I watched Shedeur very closely at Colorado. He's deadly accurate, he's tough, he can move better than people give him credit for, he's clutch and he's a leader."

Bayless also expressed his hope that Sanders would eventually receive an opportunity elsewhere to establish himself as a starting quarterback.

However, his claims about the motivations of NFL teams remain his personal assessment rather than an established explanation for Sanders ' draft slide.

Browns could give Shedeur the opportunity he needs

Sanders already has experience starting NFL games, having taken over during the closing stages of his rookie campaign in 2025.

He started seven games, finishing with three victories, seven touchdown passes and 10 interceptions before returning to a backup role this season.

Browns receiver Jerry Jeudy has expressed confidence in his teammate, highlighting his ability to create opportunities for Cleveland's passing attack.

articles.title: Is Shedeur Sanders going to be without a team? Why his personality is ruining his Browns career
articles.standfirst: An unusual exchange with reporters has brought the Cleveland quarterback's attitude back into the spotlight
articles.summary: An unusual exchange with reporters has brought the Cleveland quarterback's attitude back into the spotlight
articles.body:
S hedeur Sanders has another opportunity to change the narrative surrounding his NFL career, but his latest interaction with the media has given his critics fresh ammunition.

The Cleveland Browns quarterback attracted attention after an unusual answer during a press conference ahead of Sunday's meeting with the New Orleans Saints .

Rather than offering a straightforward response about his preparation, Sanders made a cryptic remark that quickly became a talking point among analysts and fans.

His performance in front of the cameras prompted a particularly strong reaction from NFL analyst Jay Skapinac , who suggested that Sanders could find himself without a team if his approach continues to create problems.

The criticism is especially significant because Sanders is currently trying to establish himself in Cleveland after losing the starting quarterback competition to Deshaun Watson before the 2026 season.

The 24-year-old has not had many opportunities to demonstrate his abilities this year. However, Watson's recent concussion has potentially opened the door for Sanders to take over under centre against the Saints.

Asked on ‘Fearless with Jason Whitlock’ whether he had studied New Orleans ' defence, Sanders responded: “Yeah, I seen a lot. When I smile, you know that means – something. I'm maturing, I'm maturing. I could have gave that a decent answer, but now I'm just going to smile whenever it's just like some questions.”

The response was intended to suggest that he knew more about the opposition than he wanted to reveal, but it did not go down particularly well with everyone watching.

Instead of focusing exclusively on his preparation, the conversation shifted towards his attitude and whether he understands the importance of handling the media responsibilities that come with being an NFL quarterback.

Why Sanders' personality is becoming a talking point

Skapinac's criticism reflects a wider debate about whether Sanders' public image could become an obstacle to his professional development.

The quarterback has attracted considerable attention since his college days at Colorado, where he played under his father, Deion Sanders .

His confidence and outspoken personality have helped make him one of the most recognisable young players in American football, but that attention has also brought additional scrutiny.

His fall in the 2025 NFL Draft was an early indication that not every organisation was convinced. Initially considered a potential first-round selection, Sanders eventually went to the Browns with the 144th overall pick in the fifth round.

There were several factors behind that slide, including questions about his on-field development, his handling of the pre-draft process and concerns raised by some evaluators about his personality.

His rookie campaign also gave him plenty to improve. Sanders started seven games in 2025, completing 120 of 212 passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. He also endured significant pressure, being sacked 23 times in eight appearances.

Those numbers have made it difficult for him to establish himself as an obvious long-term starter, particularly with Cleveland bringing in competition at quarterback.

There has nevertheless been support for Sanders . Former NFL analyst Skip Bayless recently argued that the quarterback had been unfairly treated during the draft process and suggested that concerns about his personality had influenced teams' decisions.

Bayless said: "What happened to Shedeur [Sanders] in his draft was the biggest draft injustice I have ever experienced… I thought he should go No. 1 to the Titans instead of Cam Ward," before adding that he "prays" Sanders gets a chance elsewhere to prove he can be an NFL starter.

The immediate challenge is to turn that opportunity into meaningful production. Sanders has appeared in two games during the 2026 regular season, completing all three of his pass attempts for just two yards.

Watson entered concussion protocol after reporting symptoms following the Browns ' defeat to Pittsburgh , leaving his availability for the Saints game uncertain. Cleveland head coach Todd Monken has therefore been preparing Sanders to step in if required.

That makes Sunday's game potentially important for the young quarterback. A convincing performance could strengthen his case for a more regular role, while another disappointing display would give the coaching staff further reason to look elsewhere.

However, the idea that Sanders is about to become completely without a team remains speculation. He is still under contract with Cleveland, and the organisation has not announced any decision to release or trade him.

Ultimately, his future will depend far more on what he produces on the field than on one awkward press conference. But with his career at an important stage, Sanders will need to show that he can handle both the football and the responsibilities that come with being an NFL quarterback.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders and the unusual problem he could face in his debut as a starter because of an NFL reporter
articles.standfirst: The Cleveland Browns quarterback is preparing for his first start of the 2026 season, but a growing dispute involving his supporters and a local reporter has created another distraction ahead of Sunday's game
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns quarterback is preparing for his first start of the 2026 season, but a growing dispute involving his supporters and a local reporter has created another distraction ahead of Sunday's game
articles.body:
S hedeur Sanders is approaching a major opportunity with the Cleveland Browns , but the attention surrounding his first start of the 2026 NFL season is not entirely focused on what he can deliver on the field.

Instead, an uncomfortable dispute involving his fanbase and a prominent Cleveland media personality has added another layer of scrutiny before Sunday's meeting with the New Orleans Saints .

The controversy emerged after reporter and radio host Anthony Lima criticised the behaviour of some Sanders supporters online. Lima claimed that criticism of the young quarterback regularly leads to personal abuse, including homophobic insults and threats of physical violence.

“I am honestly fascinated by how differently the Shedeur fans react to criticism of their QB. Been doing this a long time and have gotten called every name in the book. But his fans go right to homophobic insults and threats of physical violence. They need to be studied,” he wrote on X.

Lima's comments came amid wider debate about Sanders ' interactions with reporters during the week.

The quarterback has attracted considerable attention since entering the NFL, and his supporters have frequently defended him when journalists question his performances or conduct.

However, the allegations raised by Lima go beyond ordinary disagreements between fans and the media. While criticism of a player's performances is part of professional sport, threats directed at journalists are a separate matter and should not be treated as a normal part of online debate.

The timing is particularly awkward for Sanders , who is preparing to take on a much bigger responsibility for Cleveland.

Sanders' press conference comments add to the attention

The latest discussion began after Sanders was asked about the New Orleans defense during a media availability. Rather than offering a detailed assessment of the unit, he delivered an answer that quickly attracted attention.

“Yeah, I’ve seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means something. (laughs) I’m maturing, you know what I’m saying? I’m maturing. Like, I could have given that a decent answer, but now I’m just going to smile,” Sanders said after being asked about New Orleans’ defense.

The response was compared with that of Saints quarterback Tyler Shough , who offered a more straightforward evaluation when asked about Cleveland's defensive personnel.

Browns reporter Daryl Ruiter also reacted to the contrast, writing on X: “Oh look, Tyler Shough was asked about the #Browns defense and he wasn’t a (expletive) about it….”

One fan summed up the comparison with a short response: “Night and day.”

Sanders had already drawn attention earlier in the week after being questioned about his decision to sign with an agent during the season. The quarterback appeared irritated by the subject and responded: “What that got to do with this game?” He added: “I'm focused on this game. Anything else really don't matter at this point.”

The exchanges have renewed discussion about how Sanders handles media attention, although the reaction from some supporters has become a separate issue from the quarterback's own answers.

His opportunity to change the conversation will arrive on Sunday. Deshaun Watson entered concussion protocol after reporting symptoms following Cleveland's November 1 defeat to the Pittsburgh Steelers .

The Browns subsequently confirmed Sanders would start against New Orleans, giving the second-year quarterback his first regular-season start of 2026.

Sanders previously started seven games during his rookie campaign in 2025, completing 56.6% of his passes for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. He will now have another opportunity to demonstrate how much he has developed since that experience.

The Browns enter the matchup with a 5–3 record and need a strong performance to remain in contention in the AFC North. The Saints, meanwhile, will be looking to take advantage of the uncertainty surrounding Cleveland's quarterback situation.

For Sanders, the immediate challenge is preparing for a demanding game while the conversation around him continues to grow.

Whether he can keep the focus on football, rather than the latest dispute involving his supporters and the media, will be another part of the spotlight awaiting him in New Orleans.
